deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page sets up 'Methode aus vier Längen und zwei Breiten die Bahn eines Himmelskörpers zu berechnen'. Four geocentric longitudes α,α',α'',α''' are used, but latitudes only at the two middle dates, β' and β''. Earth's heliocentric longitudes are l..l''' and its radii R..R'''. The middle distances are reduced to z' = Δ'+R'cosδ' and z'' = Δ''+R''cosδ''. Here z is the projection of the heliocentric radius vector onto the line of sight, so r'^2 = z'^2+a'^2 with a' = R'sinδ'. These satisfy two coupled equations:
(A) z'' = -e' + d'(z'+c')/(1+b'/r'^3)
(B) z' = -e'' + d''(z''+c'')/(1+b''/r''^3)

DERIVATION OF (A) (mine). Write the planar relation r' = n r + n'' r'', with n = [r'r'']/[rr''] and n'' = [rr']/[rr'']. Project it on the ecliptic unit vector u = (-sin α, cos α, 0). This is perpendicular to the first line of sight, so the unknown ρ drops out and leaves:
R' sin(l'-α) + ρ'cosβ' sin(α'-α) = n R sin(l-α) + n''[R'' sin(l''-α) + ρ''cosβ'' sin(α''-α)].
Solving for z'' = ρ''+R''cosδ'' gives c', e' and d' as on the previous page, with:
- P' = n/n'' (first approximation (t''-t')/(t'-t));
- 1/n'' = (1+P')/(n+n'').
The dynamical relation is n+n'' = 1 + b'/r'^3 with b' = ½k²(t'-t)(t''-t') to first order; V' is Gauss's exact factor, i.e. b' = Q/2 in the notation of Theoria Motus. (B) follows symmetrically with r'' = m r' + m''' r'''.

THIS PAGE, formulas. Once z' and z'' are known, w''-w' (the heliocentric angle between r' and r'') follows. Crossing r' = n r + n'' r'' with r'' and with r gives:
(1) r sin(w''-w) = r' sin(w''-w')/n = (1+P')/[(1+b'/r'^3)P'] · r' sin(w''-w').
(2) r sin(w'-w) = (n''/n) r'' sin(w''-w') = (1/P') r'' sin(w''-w').
Together these give r and w'-w. Symmetrically, from r'' = m r' + m''' r''' with P'' = m'''/m:
(3) r''' sin(w'''-w') = (1+P'')/[(1+b''/r''^3)P''] · r'' sin(w''-w').
(4) r''' sin(w'''-w'') = (1/P'') r' sin(w''-w').
The crossed (12)/(02), (t'-t)/(t''-t') factor in (1) is a remnant of the exact sector/time form.

EXAMPLE: Uranus, 1781-1783. Times are counted in days from 1781 Jan 0: 76.4451 (17 Mar 1781), 355.7472, 631.6639, 958.6884.
- α: 84°29'33", 90°51'22", 97°13'25", 100°16'49".
- β' = 0°15'5", β'' = 0°16'50".
- l: 177°43'43", 90°51'22", 1°9'50", 324°1'14".
- log R: 9.9984480, 9.9927040, 0.0008850, 0.0050720.
- log(t'-t) = 2.4460741, log(t''-t') = 2.4407780, log(t'''-t'') = 2.5145803.
- log k = 8.2355814, so log θ = 0.6816555, 0.6763594, 0.7501617.

Auxiliary angles.
- The second observation is an exact opposition (α' = l'). So γ' = 90°, δ' = β' and cos δ' = cos β'; then R'cosδ' = 0.9833311 and log a' = log sinβ' + log R' = 7.6422221+9.9927040 = 7.6349261.
- Third observation: tan γ'' = tan β''/sin(α''-l''), with log sin(96°3'35") = 9.9975665, so γ'' ≈ 0°16'55". Also log|cos δ''| = 9.0235201 + 9.9999948 = 9.0235149, hence R''cosδ'' = -0.1057791 and δ'' = 96°3'34.735". Then log sin δ'' = 9.9975666 and log a'' = 9.9984516.

Coefficients b. log b' = log θ+log θ''-log 2 = 1.0569849 and log b'' = 1.1254911, i.e. V'M² is taken as k² in this first approximation.

Coefficient c'. Because α' = l', the term in c' reduces to c' = R'(1/cosβ' - cosβ') = R' sin²β'/cosβ'. Using 5.2844484 + 9.9927040 this gives c' = +0.00001893.

Coefficient c''. log R''/cosβ'' = 0.0008902, log sin(α'''-l'') = 9.9944793 and log cosec(α'''-α'') = 1.2730806. Their sum 1.2684501 gives 18.55453; adding 0.10578 gives c'' = 18.66031.

Terms of e'' and e'.
- log P' = 2.4407780-2.4460741 = 9.9947039 and log P'' = 9.9261977, i.e. (12)/(01) ≈ 1.
- R''' term: log R'''/cosβ' = 0.0050762, log sin(α'''-l''') = 9.8397234, log cosec(α'''-α') = 0.7858396; sum 0.6306392. Multiplied by P'' this gives 3.6044325, the variable part of e''.
- R term: 9.9984532 + 9.9993069 + 0.6568359 = 0.6545960. Multiplied by P' this gives 4.459641, the variable part of e'.

Constant parts.
- e'': -R'cosδ' + R' sin(α'''-l')/(cosβ' sin(α'''-α')), with log sin = 9.2141603. This equals c' = 0.00001893, since l' = α'. Hence e'' = 3.604451; an earlier 4.220198/4.220317 is struck out.
- e': 0.0008902 + 9.9970493n + 0.6568359 = 0.6547754n, i.e. -4.516223. Adding 0.105779 gives -4.410444. Hence e' = 0.049197; an earlier 0.601596 is struck out.

Coefficients d.
- d' = sin(α'-α)/sin(α''-α)·cosβ'/cosβ''·(1+P'): 9.0446877 + 0.6568359 + 0.0000010 = 9.7015246; plus log(1+P') = 0.2983900 gives log d' = 9.9999146.
- d'': 8.7269194 + 0.7858396 - 0.0000010 = 9.5127580; plus log(1+P'') = 0.2656948 gives log d'' = 9.7784528.

The next page solves (A)-(B) by iteration (z' ≈ 18.78, i.e. Uranus at r ≈ 18.8 AU) and then refines P, b and d.
errors: Formula (3) as written has b' in (1+b'/r''^3); by symmetry and by the definitions it must be b''.
Formula (1) writes the denominator as (z'z'+aa')^{3/2}. It should be (z'z'+a'a')^{3/2} = r'^3, a notational slip.

The previous page's d' contains an extra time/area factor (t''-t)/(t'-t)·(01)/(02) besides (1+P'). The actual computation of d' uses only sin-ratio·cos-ratio·(1+P'), which is the correct 1/n'' = (1+P')/(n+n'') with the 1/(n+n'') factor carried by 1/(1+b'/r'^3). The written d' formula is therefore inconsistent or garbled; the computation is right.

Gauss's own slips, corrected by him on this page: e'' first computed as 4.220198 / 4.220317, then corrected to 3.604451; e' first 0.601596, then corrected to 0.049197. These stem from a wrong variable part, apparently using the wrong P-multiplied term.
The labels on the page are shorthand: 'sin δ'-α' means sin(α'-α), 'sin δ''-ι'' means sin(α'''-l'), and 'R'''/cosδ'' means R'''/cosβ'. These are not computational errors.
All checked logarithms are correct to about 1e-7: log sin 6°21'49", log cosec 12°43'52", log sin 136°15'35", log|cos 96°3'35"|, log(1+P'), log(1+P''), the time logs, c', c'', d', d'', e' and e''.

results.what: Orbit determination from four longitudes and two latitudes: reduction to two coupled equations in z', z'' using P = n/n'' and b ≈ ½θθ'' (i.e. n+n''-1 ≈ θθ''/(2r'^3)).
results.modern_name: Gauss's method for four observations of which only two are complete, used for orbits of small inclination
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Theoria Motus (1809), Book II, Section II

results.what: Recovery of r, w'-w and r''', w'''-w'' from the triangle-ratio relations r sin(w''-w) = r' sin(w''-w')/n and r sin(w'-w) = (n''/n) r'' sin(w''-w').
results.modern_name: Coplanarity / triangle-area (sector-ratio) relations in Gauss's method

results.what: Worked numerical example with Uranus observations of 1781-1783 (second observation at opposition, latitudes about 15').
results.usually_credited_to: Various (Lexell, Laplace, Méchain and others for the 1781 orbit)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft (ca. Jan 1807, cf. diary entry noted on the previous page) of the method Gauss published in Theoria Motus 1809 for four observations with only two complete. It is well known as his. The only minor point of interest is the use of Uranus 1781-83 as the test example.

transcription_corrections: The table's third column '15.5' and '16.50' are the latitudes β' = 0°15'5" and β'' = 0°16'50".
The fifth table column (2.4460741, 2.4407780, 2.5145803, 8.2355814) holds the logs of t'-t, t''-t', t'''-t'' and log k. The last column holds log θ.
In formula (3) the right-hand side reads r'' sin(w''-w'), not r' sin(w''-w'); the image shows r''. The b' there should be b''.
'1+P' 0,2983400' should read 0.2983900, the value actually used in the d' computation (log 1.987879 = 0.298390).
'sin δ'-α' / 'C. sin δ'-α' mean log sin(α'-α) and its complement. 'sin δ''-ι'' means log sin(α'''-l'). 'R'''/cosδ'' means R'''/cosβ'. 'sin δ''' in that column means sin(α'''-l''').
The line 'Pars Variab.: + 3,6044325  −4,516223  +0,105779' mixes two columns. 3.6044325 is the variable part of e''; -4.516223 + 0.105779 = -4.410444 is the constant part of e'.
The first formula's denominator is written (z'z'+aa')^{3/2}; it is intended as (z'z'+a'a')^{3/2}.
The heading '1781 Jan.' means days are counted from 1781 Jan 0; the object is Uranus.
